title: The First Number Seen Twice

concept.title: Stop at the first hit
body: Scan the numbers from left to right and keep the set of numbers seen so far. The **first number that is already in the set** is the answer, and you can stop right there. Because you stop early, the work is proportional to the position of the answer, not always to `n`.
Be careful with the meaning of "first": here it is the first position where a number turns out to be a **repeat**, which is not always the same as the first number that has a copy somewhere.

statement: Read the numbers from left to right. Print the first number that you have already read before. If all numbers are different, print `none`.
outputFormat: Print the number, or the word `none`.

examples.note: The second 6 is the first repeat (the 5 repeats only later).

hints: Keep a set of the numbers read so far.
If the current number is already in the set, it is the answer.
If the scan ends without a hit, print none.

explanation: The first number found in the set of earlier numbers is the first repeat.
solution.complexity: Time O(n) on average, space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

seen = set()
answer = "none"
for x in a:
    if x in seen:
        answer = x
        break
    seen.add(x)
print(answer)
